Not final until the ChatGPT export is compared. Creator revisions remain authoritative. ## Edition II continuity guardrails - C-01 resolved: Gloin Hammerfeld is 42, Tovin Hammerfeld is 34 and is Gloin's younger brother. The creator has established these ages retroactively from the very first scene on Autumn Day 19; the older source-record inconsistency has been corrected, not preserved as alternate in-world history. Bruni is 57 and Elska 26. - The Hammerfelds are an ordinary working family with no established noble status or wealth; their precise home address, finances, family conflicts and whether Gloin has a retained room are not to be invented. - Gloin's ancestry and any First Throne relation have no predetermined answer. A possible direct descent is not proof of an existing secret lineage. - Keep all NPC knowledge compartmentalised, especially Hadrik's ignorance of the recent stone tests and independent Day 22 testimony. - These ages agree with the updated World Bible; Gloin was already 42 on Day 19. Other biographical unknowns remain open. Direct source: Characters, Families & Relationships. Historical source: The Eryndor World Bible. --- ## Complete topic reference — preserved from the preceding edition This page is the reference for established characters in Eryndor, their biographies, personalities, relationships, occupations, knowledge boundaries and current commitments. Dated actions and scene-by-scene developments belong in the separate Campaign Chronicle; this page should be updated only when campaign events establish durable character facts. ## Character canon rules - NPCs are autonomous people with their own goals, responsibilities, loyalties, relationships, limitations and lives. - NPCs only know information they have been told, personally witnessed, read in an accessible source or could reasonably discover. - Do not give a character secret knowledge merely because it would make a scene easier. - A character's species or cultural reputation is not a substitute for an individual personality. - Preserve ages, names, relationships, occupations and established history. Do not silently reconcile contradictions. - Gloin's actions, words, thoughts and intentions are controlled by the player. Never write unchosen dialogue or actions for him. - Characters can disagree, refuse, make mistakes, conceal information, change their minds, be injured or die when events warrant it. No NPC has guaranteed plot protection. ## Gloin Hammerfeld - People: Khazari dwarf. - Age: 42. - Origin: Common-born, from Karak-Varn. - Occupation: Currently unemployed; pursuing training and opportunities. - Military status: Not enlisted. - Ancestry: Unknown and intentionally unresolved. No hidden lineage, chosen-one status or predetermined destiny. - Character path: Open. Gloin may pursue combat, runesmithing, engineering, trade, exploration, politics or another path through his choices and earned progress. ### Personality and established character Gloin is outgoing and curious, increasingly courageous, ambitious without being self-assured, practical and interested in learning. He values family and humour. His confidence and abilities develop through experience; he is not automatically an expert or a legendary hero. ### Current skills and development - Beginner in combat, with no prior experience striking a person with an axe. - Accepted into Sergeant Keldrun's six-week civilian shield-and-axe course, three sessions per week. - Preliminary Deepcraft and Runecraft potential; possible Stonecalling affinity, not mastery. - Learning First Throne script. Three introductory symbols in active practical work: Hold, Within and Until Command. Day 20 source establishes that Gloin studied, copied and could recognise twelve symbols from Hadrik's book. Do not treat that book recognition as practical magic proficiency or mastery of twelve. - Beginning engineering fundamentals with Borin Ashmantle. - Developing practical Deepcraft perception through supervised exercises with Maela. His impressions are preliminary and do not prove conscious communication with stone or a reliable Stonecalling ability. - Has not yet activated a rune himself. Maela has demonstrated a basic modern Khazari warming rune. ### Earliest recovered material screening — Autumn Day 19, before 3:06 PM This is an earlier, less conclusive stage than the later controlled aptitude tests below. At Maela's Silver Anvil, Gloin held three materials: a black rune-inscribed iron piece (faint palm-to-forearm vibration and briefly glowing rune), a copper disc bearing a binding inscription (almost no effect), and a smooth mountain crystal (subtle response). Maela compared responses with her own, referred to possible stone-bound Deep Resonance sensitivity, but warned that one test cannot distinguish innate sensitivity from a particular enchantment. Her initial ratings were Runecraft: some sensitivity; Deepcraft: promising possibility; Forgebinding, Hearthmagic, Stonecalling, Ancestral Binding: untested. No magical discipline had been mastered. Maela, Borin and Hadrik also discussed whether Gloin could pursue runesmithing alongside a future military career. Borin favoured joining the Army first for discipline and engineering skills; Hadrik favoured continuing ancient studies while keeping commitments flexible; Maela offered provisional instruction two times weekly, first month without an immediate fee, and the possibility of meeting an unnamed military armourer who worked with enchantments. These were suggestions/offers; Gloin remained unemployed and not enlisted at 3:06 PM on Day 19. Later records confirm he eventually accepted study and a civilian combat course, but should not backdate those acceptances without direct source. Day 20 6:15 AM, Maela's note: The narrator showed a note slipped under Gloin's door: Keldrun would meet him “tomorrow morning” (Day 21) at the Iron Circle to assess physical condition and weapon handling before acceptance into his six-week course; bring his personal axe. This fixes the initially proposed assessment date, not a proven already-completed Day 20 lesson. The actual later assessment and course enrolment exist elsewhere in the record, but their specific turn-by-turn chronology remains to be recovered. ### Earlier controlled aptitude tests Maela's preliminary assessment recorded: - Strong potential in Deepcraft. - Strong potential in Runecraft. - Possible affinity for Stonecalling. - Forgebinding, Hearthmagic and Ancestral Binding had not been tested. During earlier controlled tests, Gloin felt a vibration like a distant heartbeat from an ancient rune, identified a cold section in a broken rune, and briefly elicited a glow from a disconnected binding stone. Maela stopped before overstressing an untrained resonance. These were preliminary signs of aptitude, not mastery or proof of a fully developed supernatural ability. Further Stonecalling tests require a proper grounding stone and controlled conditions. Gloin should not attempt uncontrolled magical experiments. Maela's broad estimate for learning runesmithing was that basic usefulness may take a few years, dependable skill around a decade, and accomplishment several decades. This is her professional estimate, not a guaranteed timetable for Gloin. ### Day 20 morning — Borin's engineering lesson and quarry discovery Gloin's first practical engineering lesson with Borin Ashmantle took place at the Old Quarry Access, beginning 7:00 AM on Autumn Day 20, not merely as a proposed appointment. Borin showed him three sections of old quarry tunnel: at 7:05, roof fractures, dampness, dust and hollow sounds; at 7:18, support pillars; at 7:26, timber supports. The main structural exercise was over around 7:45, followed by a 7:48–8:35 exploration of a survey marker and First Throne symbols. After finishing around 8:35, the two went for breakfast at 8:40 AM; costs and dialogue are not preserved in the recovered chronology. Borin's comparison with a symbol on the sealed eastern mine survey gave the old-quarry finding potential relevance, but the old quarry is not the eastern mine itself. The particular survey marker had been moved for an unknown reason. The original full dialogue remains unverified, and the two separate quarry sites in current lore are not automatically the same. Gloin remains a beginner in practical engineering despite the completed lesson. ### Day 20, 12:15 PM — Gloin and Hadrik exchange a proper introduction Although Gloin met Hadrik on Day 19 around 9:35 AM and initially chose to test Hadrik's loyalty before explaining his purpose, he did not properly give Hadrik his name during that first encounter. A prior preserved Eryndor conversation places their formal introduction at 12:15 PM on Autumn Day 20 at the Royal Historical Archive. Gloin apologised for working with him without introducing himself and said, “I'm Gloin Hammerfeld.” Hadrik joked “Gloin Hammerfeld. Well, it's about time”, reciprocated with his name, reassured Gloin that trust is earned through actions, said Gloin had demonstrated that trust, and wrote his name into the archive record. The Day 20 3:55 PM note/Varric discussion is a later meeting that same day; Hadrik correctly knew Gloin's name by then. This midday scene was found in earlier conversation history, not in the currently pasted excerpt; the complete surrounding midday dialogue still awaits primary-transcript review. The name and apology scene does not alter Gloin's age (42), ancestry, inventory, or the later Day 22 campaign pause. ### Day 20 afternoon/evening — dated study, evidence circulation, combat preparation - 3:20 PM: Gloin deliberately planned Hadrik and Maela visits plus axe preparation, with a meal first. 3:30 PM Crownward lunch cost 4 copper, with the source ledger explicitly 18 silver 93 copper remaining. - 3:55 PM: Gloin informed Hadrik of Edda's recollections, the copied Thrain note, missing authority piece and Varric Stonehelm's reported appointment authority over Dorin. Hadrik read the transcription twice, retained a copy and promised to investigate Stonehelm's service history. 4:40 PM: Gloin showed Maela the note; she did not confirm listening-network reactivation and said a future Stonecalling exam would require a prepared grounding stone. - 5:50–6:35 PM: Gloin used The Foundations of First Throne Script to copy and study the first twelve symbols, achieving recognition with occasional hesitation, not mastery or proof of using all twelve. He noted a symbol meaning “maintain” resembling a marking in the eastern mine's outer containment ring. This does not supersede the three symbols established in active beginner practice: Hold, Within and Until Command. - 6:45–7:10 PM: Gloin did solo introductory axe drills focusing on stance, weapon travel and recovery. He became sore but remained healthy; this is not completion of Keldrun's military or civilian instruction. - 7:30 PM: Barley stew, bread and cheese, no recorded payment; checked axe, boots and clothes. 9:00 PM: slept, healthy, ledger 18s 93c, not enlisted. - Day 21 6:30–6:35 AM: Gloin chose breakfast first, ahead of Keldrun's assessment; the visible source does not show breakfast or its price. At Day 20's 4:40 PM discussion, Maela proposed Runecraft instruction after the assessment. Later course and study records remain authoritative for what eventually happened, without backdating outcomes. Important purse discrepancy to audit: The source's 4-copper meal followed by 18s93c implies 18s97c beforehand if no other transaction occurred, despite the Day 19 opening's “18 silver” summary. The Day 21 supper cost 8 silver and produced a recorded 10s82c; an additional net 11 copper separates that from 18s93c after accounting for supper alone. Keep both dated ledgers; do not invent the intervening transactions. ### Last confirmed condition and resources The following is the last confirmed status at the campaign pause; update only when events occur. - Healthy and uninjured. - Wealth: 10 silver crowns and 82 copper pieces at the last confirmed balance. - Currency now has four standard denominations: 100 copper = 1 silver; 100 silver = 1 gold; 100 gold = 1 platinum. Gloin's existing ledger remains in silver and copper unless a transaction makes conversion necessary. - Inventory: ordinary clothes; leather boots with worn soles; personal axe; family keepsake (its significance is not established); borrowed copy of The Foundations of First Throne Script; notebook containing notes and survey-symbol sketches. - Borin retains the original partial survey. Gloin does not possess it. - Maela has not yet provided the name or route of the quarry that supplied her workshop granite. She agreed to retrieve old supplier records. ### Commitments and scheduled training - Maela Deepforge: Provisional runesmithing apprenticeship at the Silver Anvil, twice weekly when schedules permit. First month carries no immediate fee. Curriculum includes First Throne script, modern Khazari runic fundamentals, identifying active and dormant enchantments, magical materials and controlled practical activation. - Sergeant Keldrun Broadshield: Six-week civilian shield-and-axe course, three sessions weekly. Initial assessment: good instinct for redirecting pushes, footwork needs refinement, axe control fair, no combat experience and good discipline. Day 22's session was excused for the mine inspection. Next planned session Day 23 morning; exact time not established. - Bruni Hammerfeld: Metallurgy lesson at 11:30 AM on Autumn Day 23. Bring notebook, work clothes and gloves. First topic: ores, refining and distinguishing good stock from poor material. - Elska Hammerfeld: Discreet research into historical attempts to use ambient/Common Magic as an intermediary between disciplines. She will use public records, old works and archived accounts and report to Gloin first. The research has not yet begun; do not involve Hadrik without Gloin's choice. ## Khazari social norm — family choice, craft mastery and the duty to contribute Creator-established Khazari cultural principle: Marriage, children and mastery of a craft are independent dimensions of a dwarf's life, and none of their combinations is inherently strange or shameful. Some Khazari are legendary masters who also raise substantial families. Others live with partners and children while being perfectly competent, ordinary craftspeople without pursuing perfection. Others devote centuries to becoming masters and never form a family. Some do not choose mastery but still do honest work, maintain friendships and households, and contribute to their communities. Being unmarried, childless, married, highly skilled or unexceptional in one's trade is not itself grounds for stigma. The real cultural expectation is useful effort: A Khazari who is capable of contributing yet deliberately chooses permanent idleness and expects others to carry their burden may face disapproval, gossip and loss of respect. Dwarven culture values work, effort, service, responsibility and craft, not just extraordinary talent. A reliable journeyman, farmer, trader, clerk, cook or parent can be respected alongside a master engineer. Apprenticeship, study, running a household, raising children, caring for relatives, public service and community duties count as meaningful work; contributing need not mean wage employment or physically strenuous labour. Fairness and individual variety: Illness, disability, injury, involuntary unemployment, bereavement, age, recovery and genuine difficulty finding work are not equivalent to choosing laziness. Different Khazari individuals and clans may judge people more harshly or more generously, and a town can have internal debates about inherited wealth, early retirement or what counts as service. These are social expectations, not compulsory species instincts or a universal criminal law. Long lives and demographics: Overlapping generations and large extended families remain integral to Eryndor. Mastery and family may coexist for centuries. No birth rates, fertility biology, populations, marriage ratios or character ages change. Tolkien's isolated or unmarried craft-absorbed Dwarves are one possible archetype, not a general rule imposed on the Khazari. Gloin-specific continuity: Gloin Hammerfeld, 42, is recorded as not employed and not enlisted at the Day 19 opening, but he is actively pursuing work, instruction, research and a direction in life. Do not narrate that his family or society has branded him lazy merely because his employment status was unset; reactions require dialogue and actual behaviour in play. His family Durgan, Mara, Bruni, Tovin and Elska remains unchanged. ## Clan and family continuity — long-lived people may have large families The owner confirms that ancient, long-lived Khazari and other peoples can remain deeply invested in large families, clans, siblings, parents, descendants and multigenerational relations even while devoting centuries to craft, research or personal ambitions. The Tolkien Dwarf/Elf analogy is not permission to reduce families or weaken their relationships. The Hammerfeld family is a working-class Karak-Varn household with parents Durgan (168) and Mara (161) and their four children Bruni (57), Gloin (42), Tovin (34), Elska (26). Their relationships and the completed Day 21 family gathering remain as documented below. Neither a new fertility rate nor a universal family-size rule has been established. ## Immediate family — Hammerfeld The Hammerfelds are a common-born working family in Karak-Varn, not wealthy or politically influential. Both parents are alive. Gloin is one of four children. Family members have their own work, concerns and relationships; they do not exist solely to support Gloin. ### Durgan Hammerfeld — 168 Gloin's father. Ironworker and repair smith. Gruff, practical, stubborn and quietly dependable. Measures people by their work and whether they keep their word. Loves Gloin but rarely says so directly. Respects his curiosity while worrying that he gets involved in matters beyond his experience. ### Mara Hammerfeld — 161 Gloin's mother. Runs the household and works part-time as a textile mender and clothing repairer. Warm, perceptive and sharp-tongued when needed; difficult to fool. Affectionate but no pushover. Notices when something troubles Gloin and is likely to challenge him about sleeping rough while family is nearby. ### Bruni Hammerfeld — 57 Gloin's older sister. Apprentice armourer working toward becoming a full craftswoman. Competitive, confident, blunt, ambitious and fiercely protective beneath her teasing. She remembers Gloin as an inquisitive nuisance and gives him grief for disappearing from family life. Offers practical fabrication, armour and metallurgy help. ### Tovin Hammerfeld — 34 Gloin's younger brother. Mine maintenance worker specialising in pumps, drainage and ventilation. Sociable, good-humoured, impulsive, mechanically minded and sometimes impatient. He and Gloin share a friendly rivalry; Tovin admires Gloin's willingness to try new things but thinks he can take himself too seriously. Offers practical knowledge of pumps and ventilation. Continuity correction: Tovin is Gloin's younger brother. Their canonical ages have always been Gloin 42 and Tovin 34, including on Day 19. The old mismatched entry was corrected retroactively. ### Elska Hammerfeld — 26 Gloin's youngest sister. Errand-runner and junior clerk at a local merchant's counting house. Clever, observant, curious, quietly mischievous and a good listener. Looks up to Gloin more than she admits. She has agreed to conduct discreet research for him into historical uses of ambient/Common Magic as an intermediary between disciplines. ## Extended family — Coppervein ### Harn Coppervein — 174 Gloin's maternal uncle and Mara's older brother. Retired stonecutter who takes occasional measuring and repair jobs. Patient, dry-humoured and opinionated about workmanship. Treats Gloin as capable of more than he gives himself credit for, but expects him to prove it. ### Vessa Coppervein — 158 Harn's wife. Baker attached to a neighbourhood provisions shop. Sociable, practical, generous with food and an enthusiastic collector of local gossip. Fond of Gloin. ### Rurik Coppervein — 39 Harn and Vessa's son; Gloin's cousin. Cartwright's assistant. Easygoing, competitive and fond of joking at Gloin's expense. They grew up seeing one another regularly, though work and adulthood have made visits less frequent. ## Teachers, mentors and scholarly contacts ### Maela Deepforge — 143 Khazari master runesmith and architectural historian. Silver-grey hair tightly braided back with small metal rings in the braids. Runs The Silver Anvil in the Upper Artisan Quarter. Expert in ancient runic construction, containment architecture, magical materials and runesmithing. Blunt, practical, respected and no-nonsense, with occasional dry humour. She is Gloin's provisional runesmithing teacher and the specialist contracted for the eastern mine inspection. She accepted Veyron's inspection contract under conditions recorded in the campaign record. Maela is discreet and politically aware. She distinguishes observed evidence from interpretation, is careful not to overstate magical conclusions and does not disclose sensitive mine findings to people who have not been told. ### Borin Ashmantle Older Khazari with a grey beard and two missing fingers on his left hand. Former mining engineer and apprentice during the original eastern mine sealing. Childhood acquaintance of Gloin; practical, cautious, protective and loyal. Borin retains the original partial survey hidden at his home. On Autumn Day 19, 8:05 AM, he displayed three old survey parchments to Gloin at his residence and later hid their wooden case under a loose workshop floorboard when Edrik Voss arrived. He teaches Gloin engineering fundamentals: structural weaknesses, tunnel safety, supports, airflow, seepage, tools and surveying. He has not committed to entering the mine. He remembers Thrain's wrapped iron object and the unidentified fourth official from the original sealing. Recovered Day 19 biographical context: Borin was at the Copper Anvil alehouse at 7:35 AM, warned Gloin away from the mine and admitted he had lied to a Royal Mining Office visitor about retaining the survey. He recalled having a wife and two young daughters around the time of the sealing; their present status is not established by that recollection. Borin was an apprentice who helped seal the lower access but never claimed to have entered the buried chamber. He knew missing engineer Orik Feldspar personally. He asked Gloin not to name Edrik Voss to Hadrik before they knew they could trust the scholar. Gloin explicitly chose to hide in the workshop and overhear Voss rather than flee. ### Hadrik Ironvein — approximately 176 Khazari scholar and senior researcher at the Royal Historical Archive. Has worked there for 112 years and studied First Throne history for roughly 40 years. Careful and intellectually honest, loyal to Khazari people and history but not blindly loyal to the Crown. Research into First Throne history was administratively restricted about 40 years ago. Lent Gloin The Foundations of First Throne Script. Investigating the private repository and an obscured access-register name. Hadrik believes the First Throne may have been escaping something beneath its civilisation, but has no definitive answer. First verified on-screen meeting with Gloin: Autumn Day 19, approximately 9:35 AM, when Borin brought Gloin to Hadrik's private reading chamber in the Royal Historical Archive. Hadrik greeted Borin, “Ashmantle! I thought you were dead”; Borin replied, “Not yet.” At that instant Hadrik had not been told about Borin's survey. This must not be conflated with the Day 22 11:25 AM archive meeting, where the campaign is currently paused. Newly recovered first-conversation evidence — Autumn Day 19, 9:38 AM: Gloin explicitly chose to keep the mine investigation vague and assess Hadrik's loyalties before disclosing details. Hadrik stated he had worked at the archive for 112 years and devoted 40 years to sensitive periods of Khazari history. He said he had served three kings, regarded kings and governments as temporary, and placed his primary allegiance in Karak-Varn, the Khazari people and their historical heritage. He said a good king should tolerate criticism and denounced hiding truth to protect noble reputations. These are Hadrik's declared values; his sincerity and private alliances are not omnisciently proven. He told Gloin his First Throne inquiries had been administratively suspended about 40 years before because royal archivists objected to contradictions he found between official histories and older inscriptions; he reported no criminal case or trial. He argued that surviving First Throne institutions may have been deliberately erased politically from history to prevent a rival claim to legitimacy. This is his interpretation, and he expressly did not claim a surviving heir or legally valid claimant was identified. He said he had buried friends who asked dangerous questions, had family, students and a professional position to consider, but would not knowingly risk Khazari welfare merely to spare a noble family embarrassment. He suspected Gloin and Borin were hiding the real purpose of their visit, saying “Neither of you has come here simply to discuss history,” and volunteered to hear of a mountain threat. At the end of the screenshots, Hadrik still had not been given the actual survey, Edrik's account or mine details in this conversation. The rest of his dialogue and Gloin's next decision have not yet been supplied. ### Sergeant Keldrun Broadshield — approximately 187 Veteran Khazari infantryman with more than a century of military experience. Specialises in shield fighting, one-handed axes and hammers, formation combat, confined tunnels and defence against larger opponents. Teaches at The Iron Circle. Has accepted Gloin into a six-week civilian course. His initial assessment found promising instincts for balance and redirection, footwork needing refinement, fair axe control, untested power and good discipline. ## Historical and mine-related contacts ### Edda Coppervein Older female dwarf and granddaughter of Thrain Coppervein. Lives in the Lower Artisan District. Keeps Thrain's old possessions and the original parchment note attributed to him. Allowed Gloin to copy the note; the original remains with the family. Remembers family stories about Thrain's missing iron object and his disagreement with Orik. ### Edrik Voss — approximately 60 Deputy Examiner of the Royal Mining Office. Black trimmed beard, scar from right ear to jaw, silver royal mining signet; an educated northern accent was described by Borin. His apparent age of approximately 60 was Borin's estimate, not a verified birth record. His first known visit to Borin was 27 days before Autumn Day 19. On Day 19 at approximately 8:44 AM, Edrik returned in a dark-blue travelling coat with one unnamed armed royal guard, demanded the ninth-level survey, spoke of Thrain's unusual measurements and said Thrain had no official death record. He threatened to return in two days and warned Borin against discussing the case. Gloin overheard the meeting in hiding; Edrik glanced toward the workshop, but the scene does not confirm Edrik saw or identified Gloin. Edrik said the western wall was breached 11 nights before Autumn Day 19, watchmen heard three knocks and voices they did not understand, and “something came through”. He said the Crown wanted the matter contained and that King Durgan had not been informed, with the investigation handled under Veyron. His intentions and the accuracy of his claims remain unresolved. ### Lord Chancellor Veyron Senior political official. His office ordered restricted historical reviews and commissioned Maela's mine inspection. According to Edrik, the Royal Mining Office is acting under Veyron's authority. Veyron's motives and the King's knowledge remain unresolved; no conspiracy is established. ### Captain Roderic Vale Commander of the royal security detail assigned to Maela's inspection. Maela has not worked with him and does not know his purpose beyond command of the security detail. Further character details are unknown. ## Eastern mine inspection personnel ### Rennik Varn Eastern mine site supervisor. Responsible for the inspection site and its schedule. Can be defensive or irritated when procedures disrupt his work, but prioritises the site schedule. Knows official maintenance reports; do not assume he knows restricted ancient history or has malicious intent. ### Feldin Structural assessor. Stocky dwarf with a closely trimmed brown beard. Practical, experienced and friendly. Identifies structural distinctions and possible altered masonry, but is careful not to call an uncertain feature a doorway or hidden chamber without evidence. ### Orsa Resonance and material assessor. Thinner dwarf who carries a leather instrument case. Methodical and honest about the limits of the instruments. Uses a brass resonance gauge and can record changes, but cannot by itself identify whether a source is magical, mechanical or geological. ### Darrik Stonehand Off-duty watchman. Broad-shouldered, weathered face, dark beard streaked with grey. Independently reported three irregular knocks beyond the western boundary wall, faint whispering without words, brief scraping and a cold patch near old boundary markers. Did not hear the low hum reported by Harnel. ### Harnel Darrik's watch partner. Heard the three irregular knocks beyond the western wall, but no voices. Independently recalled faint scraping, a cold draught near the markers, a low hum lasting roughly three to four seconds after checking the wall, and a thin line of dust near the markers the following morning. He did not report a pile of dust. Served watches for 11 years and had not heard similar knocks. ## Other established or mentioned contacts ### Thuldren Maela's first Deepcraft instructor. Maela studied architecture, stonework and Runecraft before learning Deepcraft from him. He taught her to distinguish sensing from understanding. Further details are not established. ## Relationships and knowledge boundaries - The Hammerfeld family learned the mine and First Throne details because Gloin disclosed them during the Day 21 family supper. Other characters do not know those details unless they were separately told or could reasonably discover them. - Maela is discreet and does not reveal sensitive mine findings in front of people who do not know them. - Elska's ambient/Common Magic research is separate from Hadrik's historical repository work. Gloin does not want Hadrik involved in Elska's task unless he later chooses otherwise. - Darrik and Harnel gave separate accounts before comparing details. Preserve the differences between what each heard. - Hadrik's beliefs about the First Throne are interpretations, not secret knowledge of what lies behind the eastern mine door. - NPCs may have information unknown to Gloin, but the narrator must establish a plausible source before revealing it. ## Open biographical details Do not invent the following without developing them in play: - Exact ages, family histories or physical appearances not recorded above. - Full family finances, debts, home address or property ownership. - Any further biographical details about Tovin and Gloin not yet established. - Hadrik's final repository findings and the identity of the obscured register name. - Veyron's motives or the King's actual knowledge. - Captain Roderic Vale's personal background or reasons for assignment. - Thuldren's later life, current location or other students.
